title: Risk and Insurance: Perspectives on Fertility and Agrarian Change in India and Bangladesh
why: Founding statement of the children-as-insurance motive; the Arm S theory anchor.

title: Fertility as an Adjustment to Risk
why: Arm S mechanism, stated as a risk-buffering rather than an old-age claim - the Wall 1 distinction in its original form.

title: Children as insurance
why: Formalises the insurance motive; short generic title, expect resolver trouble.

title: The Old-Age Security Motive for Fertility
why: DECOY, expected to route to C.3.c. This is the Wall 1 test case: if the Arm S literature is all shaped like this, Arm S is C.3.c's.

title: Credit Programs for the Poor and Reproductive Behavior in Low-Income Countries: Are the Reported Causal Effects the Result of Heterogeneity Bias?
why: Microcredit and reproductive behaviour, with the identification problem named in the title. Closest thing to an Arm S/composite gold record.

title: The Miracle of Microfinance? Evidence from a Randomized Evaluation
why: Composite access, RCT. Fertility may be a secondary outcome or absent - which is itself the measurement.

title: Estimating the Impact of Microcredit on Those Who Take It Up: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment in Morocco
why: Same family as Banerjee; probing whether the microcredit RCT wave measured fertility at all.

title: Microcredit Impacts: Evidence from a Randomized Microcredit Program Placement Experiment by Compartamos Banco
why: As above.

title: The Impacts of Microfinance: Evidence from Joint-Liability Lending in Mongolia
why: As above.

title: Savings Constraints and Microenterprise Development: Evidence from a Field Experiment in Kenya
why: Saving-pure access. Outcome is enterprise, not fertility - a Wall 6 boundary probe.

title: Banking the poor via savings accounts: Evidence from a field experiment
why: Saving-pure access with household outcomes; probe for a fertility or birth-spacing outcome.

title: Do Rural Banks Matter? Evidence from the Indian Social Banking Experiment
why: The canonical staggered branch-expansion design. Outcome is poverty; the probe asks whether anyone has run it on fertility.

title: The Real Impact of Improved Access to Finance: Evidence from Mexico
why: Branch-expansion family, outcome income and employment. Boundary probe.

title: Consumption Smoothing, Migration, and Marriage: Evidence from Rural India
why: Risk-coping through family structure where formal insurance is absent; marriage not fertility, so a Wall 6 case.

title: Demand for children in low income countries
why: Handbook chapter; theory stream, and a citation hub for Arm S.

title: Monetary Policy and Birth Rates: The Effect of Mortgage Rate Pass-Through on Fertility
why: INHERITED from C.2.c as OFF_CREDIT_C3e. Interest-rate shock at fixed house prices - the cleanest Arm B design in the inherited set.

title: The Babies of Mortgage Market Deregulation
why: INHERITED from C.2.c. Credit-supply deregulation, fertility outcome in the title. First author unknown to this candidate list - resolver supplies it.

title: Can stimulating ownership increase fertility
why: ROUTED HERE EXPLICITLY by C.2.c on 2026-07-31 and already extracted there: +2.73pp on a 0.1314 baseline. Down payment ratios, interest rates and loan ceilings move; prices do not.

title: More Credit, More Babies? Bank Credit Expansion, House Prices, and Fertility
why: INHERITED. VERSION PAIR - see the anchor log. Two DOIs, one author, and C.2.c's stored snapshot has the 2023 title as 'More Credit, FEWER Babies?'. Treat as ONE study and settle the version of record before extracting.

title: More Credit, Fewer Babies? Bank Credit Expansion, House Price, and Fertility
why: The earlier version of the record above, under C.2.c's stored title. Listed separately ONLY so the pair is visible; it is not a second study.

title: Interest Rates, House Prices, Fertility, and the Macroeconomy
why: INHERITED from C.2.c.

title: The Baby Boom: Predictability in House Prices and Interest Rates
why: INHERITED. Likely REVERSE direction (fertility to prices); kept so the direction is decided rather than assumed.

title: Fertility choice in a life cycle model with idiosyncratic uninsurable earnings risk
why: Quantitative life-cycle model with borrowing constraints; theory stream and the C.5.a boundary in model form.

title: Do Family Wealth Shocks Affect Fertility Choices? Evidence from the Housing Market
why: DECOY, expected to route to C.2.c under Wall 2. This is the study Ruling 2 struck from C.3.e's seminal list; it is here to confirm the wall fires.

title: House prices and birth rates: The impact of the real estate market on the decision to have a baby
why: DECOY, expected C.2.c. Same first author as the ReStud Arm B anchor, which makes it a sharp test that the wall routes on variation and not on author or topic.

title: Cooperatives as information machines: German rural credit cooperatives 1883-1914
why: PROBE for the historical FDT cell - savings and credit institution founding dates against parish fertility. If this cell is empty, Arm S has no FDT evidence and the demsig for FDT is NOT ASSESSED.
